content:
Yesterday when Apple announced the Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip, there was good news: the starting price remains the same as the M4 Max Mac Studio, at US$2,499.

However, if you want to upgrade the GPU, the upgrade fee has a hidden catch — the actual cost is US$300 more than the price initially shown on Apple's website…

Even John Gruber got caught out; when he was putting together the various configuration prices for the new machine yesterday, he was tripped up by this hidden upgrade fee.

The base configuration of this machine comes with an 18-core CPU and a 32-core GPU. Apple subsequently listed the option to upgrade to a 40-core GPU, clearly indicating a US$300 upcharge.

The trap is that when you select this option, the memory is also automatically boosted from 32GB to 48GB, requiring an additional US$300. Because upgrading the GPU cores forces you to also upgrade to 48GB of memory, the actual upgrade cost is double the listed price — US$600.

Apple does hint at this somewhat vaguely when you select the chip upgrade.

Have you been tempted to pick up a new Mac Mini or Mac Studio model? Let us know in the comments.
